governance_posts.title: [Discussion] Onboard cBTC (tacBTC) to Aave V3 Core and Aave V4 Core
governance_posts.description:
Author: z0r0z (ross)
Date: 2026-11-23

Summary

This post introduces cBTC, a BTC token on Ethereum backed by locks held in self-custody on Bitcoin. We are asking whether the community and service providers would support onboarding its public ERC-20, tacBTC, to the Aave V3 Core Instance, the Aave V4 Core Hub, or both. We have no preference between the two and would follow the service providers.

Motivation

cBTC has been live on Ethereum mainnet since 2026-09-18. To mint it, the owner of the BTC creates a lock on Bitcoin, and a wstETH escrow of at least 1.5x the lock’s value is posted against it. The locker keeps the key. No custodian or committee holds the BTC.

The backing can be read on-chain. At block 26,478,414 the pool’s cbtcBackingSats() returns 22,252,699 sats, the reflection-attested total of live locks. The pool has no proxy, upgrade path, pause switch or admin key over escrow, exits or payouts.

Holders can keep cBTC as the public ERC-20 tacBTC or as a confidential note inside the pool. For Aave it would be a BTC collateral whose backing is verifiable on-chain and whose custody stays with the owner of the BTC.

Specification

Contracts: ConfidentialPool, CollateralEngine, tacBTC. Risk parameters and final configuration are for the Risk Service Providers to set.

How it works

  1. The BTC owner creates a lock on Bitcoin. The coins stay in an output the owner controls.
  2. Bitcoin’s state is proven on Ethereum with SP1 zk proofs of Bitcoin proof of work. Relayers are not trusted, and anyone can prove.
  3. cBTC is minted for the lock’s value, less a fee, once the escrow is posted. Anyone can fund the escrow.
  4. If a lock is spent without a redeem, the pool sees it and the escrow can be slashed into the insurance reserve by anyone. After a proven redeem, the escrow returns to its funder.

Supply is bounded by the reflected locks. The spec is SPEC section 5.7.

What you trust

  • Bitcoin and Ethereum consensus, SP1 and Groth16 soundness, and the sp1-helios sync committee.
  • Price feeds for escrow sizing: Chainlink BTC/USD and ETH/USD, and Lido’s wstETH rate, composed into a BTC-per-wstETH feed.
  • The ops multisig (2-of-5, one-hour delay) for the CollateralEngine, within on-chain bounds: escrow ratio between 1x and 10x, notice before borrower-adverse changes, and a minimum escrow grace window of 3 days. It can set oracle and CDP parameters, drive escrow enforcement and draw on the insurance reserve.

The lock is enforced economically, not by Bitcoin script: the locker holds the key and the escrow makes spending the lock unprofitable. If a script-enforced lock is proven for a tradable token, we would move to it. The pool lineage allows this through successor pools that users opt into.

Comparison with Babylon’s Trustless Bitcoin Vaults

Babylon’s column is taken from their docs.

cBTC Babylon TBV
What it is A token that moves and trades freely, public or inside a confidential pool A collateral record for one depositor’s vault
Lock enforcement Owner’s key plus a wstETH escrow of at least 1.5x at mint, slashable Bitcoin script with pre-signed spend paths and a zk proof verified through BABE, with a challenge period of about three days
Capital cost The wstETH escrow No depositor bond is described. The docs mention a claimer’s bond in the dispute process, with no amounts
Participants Anyone can prove, fund an escrow or slash Challengers are a static, permissioned registry. Direct-redemption liquidation is permissioned. The LLP liquidation path is permissionless
Transferable Yes The record is transfer-restricted to the Aave adapter: “There is no secondary market.”
Fungible Yes No. Each vault is one UTXO, segregated
Apps Anything that takes an ERC-20 Bound to one app at creation, with an adapter per app
Status Mainnet since 2026-09-18 Testnet per the docs as of Nov 23. Mainnet is targeted for Q4 2026, in phases

TBV gives a depositor a position in one app. cBTC is a token that can be held and used anywhere, and the escrow is the cost of that.

Where it is today

  • tacBTC public supply is 70,405 sats. Most cBTC is held in the pool as confidential notes.
  • 4,876 cUSD is borrowed against cBTC.
  • tacBTC has no deep on-chain pool. We would like input on how delegates and LPs want to bootstrap one.
  • Review history is in audit/AUDITS.md. The bug bounty is in SECURITY.md.

Disclaimer

We build Tacit and cBTC. This is our own asset, and we are not compensated by anyone for this post.

Next steps

  1. Gather community feedback in this thread. We will answer questions about the design.
  2. If a service provider is open to sponsoring it, Risk and Technical Service Providers post their assessments covering supply caps, rates and oracle for V3, V4 or both. We will provide what they need.
  3. If the response is positive, move to an ARFC, then Snapshot and an AIP.

The backing can be read on-chain. At block 26,478,414 the pool’s cbtcBackingSats() returns 22,252,699 sats, the reflection-attested total of live locks. The pool has no proxy, upgrade path, pause switch or admin key over escrow, exits or payouts.

Holders can keep cBTC as the public ERC-20 tacBTC or as a confidential note inside the pool. For Aave it would be a BTC collateral whose backing is verifiable on-chain and whose custody stays with the owner of the BTC.

Specification

Contracts: ConfidentialPool, CollateralEngine, tacBTC. Risk parameters and final configuration are for the Risk Service Providers to set.

How it works

  1. The BTC owner creates a lock on Bitcoin. The coins stay in an output the owner controls.
  2. Bitcoin’s state is proven on Ethereum with SP1 zk proofs of Bitcoin proof of work. Relayers are not trusted, and anyone can prove.
  3. cBTC is minted for the lock’s value, less a fee, once the escrow is posted. Anyone can fund the escrow.
  4. If a lock is spent without a redeem, the pool sees it and the escrow can be slashed into the insurance reserve by anyone. After a proven redeem, the escrow returns to its funder.

Supply is bounded by the reflected locks. The spec is SPEC section 5.7.

What you trust

  • Bitcoin and Ethereum consensus, SP1 and Groth16 soundness, and the sp1-helios sync committee.
  • Price feeds for escrow sizing: Chainlink BTC/USD and ETH/USD, and Lido’s wstETH rate, composed into a BTC-per-wstETH feed.
  • The ops multisig (2-of-5, one-hour delay) for the CollateralEngine, within on-chain bounds: escrow ratio between 1x and 10x, notice before borrower-adverse changes, and a minimum escrow grace window of 3 days. It can set oracle and CDP parameters, drive escrow enforcement and draw on the insurance reserve.

The lock is enforced economically, not by Bitcoin script: the locker holds the key and the escrow makes spending the lock unprofitable. If a script-enforced lock is proven for a tradable token, we would move to it. The pool lineage allows this through successor pools that users opt into.

Comparison with Babylon’s Trustless Bitcoin Vaults

Babylon’s column is taken from their docs.

cBTC Babylon TBV
What it is A token that moves and trades freely, public or inside a confidential pool A collateral record for one depositor’s vault
Lock enforcement Owner’s key plus a wstETH escrow of at least 1.5x at mint, slashable Bitcoin script with pre-signed spend paths and a zk proof verified through BABE, with a challenge period of about three days
Capital cost The wstETH escrow No depositor bond is described. The docs mention a claimer’s bond in the dispute process, with no amounts
Participants Anyone can prove, fund an escrow or slash Challengers are a static, permissioned registry. Direct-redemption liquidation is permissioned. The LLP liquidation path is permissionless
Transferable Yes The record is transfer-restricted to the Aave adapter: “There is no secondary market.”
Fungible Yes No. Each vault is one UTXO, segregated
Apps Anything that takes an ERC-20 Bound to one app at creation, with an adapter per app
Status Mainnet since 2026-09-18 Testnet per the docs as of Nov 23. Mainnet is targeted for Q4 2026, in phases

TBV gives a depositor a position in one app. cBTC is a token that can be held and used anywhere, and the escrow is the cost of that.

Where it is today

  • tacBTC public supply is 70,405 sats. Most cBTC is held in the pool as confidential notes.
  • 4,876 cUSD is borrowed against cBTC.
  • tacBTC has no deep on-chain pool. We would like input on how delegates and LPs want to bootstrap one.
  • Review history is in audit/AUDITS.md. The bug bounty is in SECURITY.md.

We build Tacit and cBTC. This is our own asset, and we are not compensated by anyone for this post.
